nodes.text:
Heads-up before the A/B: this turn came back as read-only, so the low-end EQ write could not be committed. Here is exactly where the chain stands.

Done and verified
- Observation on the bass track is complete. Evidence: the bass is the project's dominant low-frequency source — bass band energy ≈56.5 dB, sub ≈48.7 dB, low-mid ≈42.5 dB, versus mid ≈31.9 dB and presence ≈11.8 dB. Track level ≈-30.3 dBFS RMS, peak ≈-15.9 dBFS, headroom ≈15.9 dB, centered (balance ≈-1.5 dB, correlation ≈0.69). So the low end is genuinely heavy/stacked rather than thin — a gentle trim was the right direction, not a boost.
- An admitted static EQ is loaded and live on the bass track: API-550A Stereo, instance id 1040 (rack node 1039), verified present in refreshed project state.
- I read its live control surface twice so the move would be made against the real instance rather than an assumed plugin.

What was blocked, and why
- Writing the low-band gain directly was refused: the parameter belongs to the live static-EQ topology, so the raw-parameter path is not legal for it.
- Routing the same move through the typed EQ path was also refused: ordinary Agent EQ mutations require a validated semantic EQ action (frozen proposal + authorization) rather than a direct call.
- I then emitted that semantic EQ action — one gentle low-shelf trim, 90 Hz, about -2 dB, with the constraint kept explicit that the bass must not lose body or go thin — but this turn was finalized as discussion/read-only, so it was not frozen or executed.

Net result: nothing was changed. The bass track still sounds exactly as it did before (the API-550A is instantiated but not yet cutting anything), so there is no A/B delta to audition yet. The direction and dose are settled and evidence-backed (trim ≈2 dB in the low shelf around 90 Hz); it only needs the turn to run with mutation authority so the action can be frozen and applied, after which you can A/B against bypass.
